children: Bone Biologics reported a net loss of $618K in the third quarter of 2026, compared with a $667K loss in the prior-year quarter, as it continued development work on its NELL-1 bone graft program.
Net loss was $618K in 3Q 2026, compared with $667K in 3Q 2025; the loss narrowed 7.4% year over year.
Diluted loss per share was $0.17 in 3Q 2026, compared with $0.37 in 3Q 2025.
Net loss for the first nine months of 2026 was $2.16M, compared with $2.42M in the prior-year period, a reduction of 11.0%.
NB1, a NELL-1/DBM bone graft, is being evaluated in an Australian pilot study involving up to 30 spinal-fusion patients. Six Australian hospital sites are under agreement to participate.
The pilot is assessing safety, bone fusion, pain, function and adverse events. The FDA has indicated that NELL-1/DBM is a combination product requiring PMA approval before U.S. commercialization.
Quarterly research and development spending rose 29% as the company worked to extend NELL-1 protein shelf life and prepare for a future pivotal study.
Management expects continued substantial investment in NELL-1 development and said available cash is expected to fund operations through the second quarter of 2027.
